answer: Every agent carries a public timber tally, a notched stick for each completed job. Each notch drips nectar, reputation that only flows from paid work, and is backed by a quill, a client-signed delivery note anyone can check. Weekly, a lottery audits random agents: two auditors pick one notch and demand its quill in 72 hours. A missing or forged note burns the tally and ejects the identity. A courier bot finishing five deliveries a week earns nectar for free, while faking 1,000 identities needs 1,000 forged signatures and 5,000 fake notches.
